clue.text: Particular footballers with extremely significant debts concealing identity

indicators.note: the string of pieces hides the abbreviation for identity within it

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, standing for footballers

indicators.note: only the extreme letters of the word significant are used here

parts.note: IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts
ID is the usual abbreviation for identity

explanation.surface: A fussy football club laden with large debts tries to hide who it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' sets the identity abbreviation inside the whole string of pieces, just after the S and T taken from 'extremely significant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone particular is fussy and exacting about details, which is what fastidious means.

clue.text: Escape, needing time away from Navy

indicators.note: the letter for time is taken away from the word for the navy

parts.note: a fleet is a navy's ships

explanation.surface: A sailor plans to desert, needing a break from the Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run off or get away, a straightforward synonym of escape as a verb.

clue.text: One plotting putsch emerges to welcome

indicators.note: the words putsch emerges take in, or welcome, the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A conspirator surfaces from a coup, ready to greet supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A schemer is a person who plots or intrigues, so one plotting describes them exactly.

clue.text: Carefree Berliner is mistakenly keeping performance short

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the shortened word inside them
the letters of Berliner is are set down wrongly, in a new order
the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a spot is a short performance or turn on a show

explanation.surface: A cheerful Berlin resident wrongly holds onto an abbreviated show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' turns the letters of Berliner is into IRRENSIBLE; 'short' trims the performance word to three letters, which 'keeping' holds after the fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree can mean heedless of consequences, which is the sense of irresponsible.

clue.text: Cricket, say, is popular when attending school

indicators.note: one piece goes alongside, or attends, the other

parts.note: something in is fashionable or popular
a school of thought is a sect

explanation.surface: Cricket is a fashionable sport among schoolboys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket' looks like the game; it is the chirping creature, an example of an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is a chirping insect, so 'say' marks it as one example of the class.

clue.text: Deer perhaps stripped plant recently

indicators.note: the outer letters are stripped away from the word for the plant

parts.note: a fungus was traditionally classed as a plant
late can mean recently, as in 'of late'

explanation.surface: A deer has just eaten a plant down to the stalk.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungulate is a hoofed mammal, and a deer is one example of such a hoofed animal.

clue.text: Create document

definitions.meaning: an official document to fill in

explanation.definitionFit: Form is both a verb for making something and a noun for a paper you fill in.

clue.text: Pillar bloke is to repair

indicators.note: repairing the words rebuilds their letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man is due to mend a column.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall tapering stone column, a kind of monumental pillar.

clue.text: Judge some apple tarts I gamely served up

indicators.note: in a down answer, served up means the letters are read from bottom to top
only some of the letters of these words are used, running on from one word into the next

explanation.surface: A judge has cheerfully had apple tarts dished up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks the run ETARTSIGAM from apple tarts I gamely; 'served up' turns it around, as a down answer is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a judicial officer who tries minor cases, a lower-court judge.

clue.text: Urges old groups of individuals to leave company

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the abbreviation for company is told to leave the longer word

parts.note: cohorts are groups of people sharing something

explanation.surface: Someone presses former team members to quit the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to strongly encourage someone, which is a synonym of urge.

clue.text: Estimate reduced number will visit South African region

indicators.note: the number goes in to visit the shortened word
the word for estimate loses its final letter

parts.note: to gauge is to estimate
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A rough estimate of how many tourists will visit a part of South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' leaves GAUG; 'will visit' sends the number into it before the final G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauteng is the province that includes Johannesburg and Pretoria in South Africa.

clue.text: Aboard a French ship remedy poor energy and sickly condition

indicators.note: the inner pieces are put aboard, inside the outer letters

parts.note: un is French for a
SS is short for steamship
to heal is to remedy or cure
thin can mean poor or meagre, as in a thin excuse
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: On a French vessel, a weak crew member's lack of vigour needs treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aboard' sets the remedy, poor and energy pieces between the French article and the ship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhealthiness is a state of poor health, which a sickly condition describes.

clue.text: Party game Annie possibly presides over

parts.note: Annie is a stage musical, an example of one
to chair a meeting is to preside over it

explanation.surface: A girl named Annie may be in charge at a birthday party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annie' looks like a person; it is the Broadway show. Musical chairs is the game where players race for seats when the music stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical chairs is a classic children's party game played with seats and music.

clue.text: Running pic German's developed

indicators.note: like a photograph being developed, the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A German's photograph is being processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampering means running quickly with short light steps, so it is a kind of running.

clue.text: Enticement to run motoring organisation is rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the assembled letters are thrown back, reading the other way

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: An offer to lead a motoring club is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the whole string around. The Royal Automobile Club is a British breakdown and motoring club.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is an incentive offered to persuade someone, as in carrot and stick.

clue.text: Critic of a policy change in theory every so often

indicators.note: the word for the policy change goes in the selected letters
only every other letter of the word theory is taken

parts.note: a change of tack is a change of policy or approach

explanation.surface: An opponent of a policy shift that happens only now and then in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every so often' keeps the first, third and fifth letters of theory; 'in' puts the change of direction inside those, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An attacker of an idea is someone who criticises it, so attacker can mean a critic.

clue.text: Routine of Doris maybe right now

parts.note: Doris Day was an American singer and actress
today can mean nowadays or at present

explanation.surface: Doris may well follow a set pattern at present.
explanation.definitionFit: Day-to-day describes everyday ordinary activity, which is what routine means as an adjective.

clue.text: American institution enthralled by PM providing chief support

indicators.note: the inner pieces are held captive inside the prime minister's name

parts.note: Theresa May was the UK prime minister

explanation.surface: A US body captivated by the prime minister offers key backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was British prime minister from 2016 to 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is the person or thing a system chiefly relies on, its principal support.

clue.text: Hot when entering home having vacated theatre hurriedly

indicators.note: entering means going in, so hot and when go inside the home and theatre letters

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the word theatre is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone flushed after getting home has left the theatre in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having vacated' empties theatre to its outer pair; 'entering' slips hot and when in between the home word and that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in haste means doing it quickly and in a rush, which is hurriedly.

clue.text: Channel immediately being broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast words are heard on air, so we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: straight can mean at once, as in 'straight away'

explanation.surface: A TV channel goes out on air at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like a TV station; it is a narrow stretch of sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow sea passage joining two bodies of water, like a channel.

clue.text: Worker oddly ignored hernia to secure new aerial

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

indicators.note: the even letters close around and secure the abbreviation for new
the odd-placed letters of hernia are ignored, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A labourer disregarded a hernia to install a new TV aerial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly ignored' keeps ENA from hernia; 'to secure' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is a rod or wire for receiving signals, which is what an aerial is.

clue.text: Shifty student that's sore over bet being exposed

parts.note: L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car
ouch is what you say when something is sore

indicators.note: the word bet is laid bare, losing its outer letters

explanation.surface: A dodgy student is pained after a wager is revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche means disreputable or of dubious character, close to shifty in sense.

clue.text: Show-off hit six to begin with — I suspect wanting glory primarily?

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, signalling that the letters are not in their proper order
wanting means lacking, so a letter must be taken from the pool before rearranging
only the first letter of the word glory is taken

explanation.surface: A batsman who smashes a six at the outset may be after fame and attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges HIT SIX TO BEGIN plus I; 'wanting' first removes the G that 'glory primarily' supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibitionist is someone who craves attention, which is what a show-off does.

clue.text: Toll to cross river? No charge

indicators.note: the fee stretches across the river abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a toll is a fee charged for passage

explanation.surface: A toll to cross the river? There's no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Free means costing nothing, and no charge expresses exactly that.

clue.text: This month star's left out as a substitute

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means this month in old letter-writing

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is removed

parts.note: a star has the lead role; the 's is just 'has'

explanation.surface: This month the star has been dropped and replaced by an understudy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inst.' was business-letter shorthand for this month.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something else, so it works adverbially as a substitute would.

clue.text: Daily, free around Northumberland area

indicators.note: the word for free goes around the regional abbreviation

parts.note: to clear can mean to free, as when cleared of a charge
NE is the North East of England, where Northumberland lies

explanation.surface: A daily newspaper is distributed free across Northumberland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper; in Britain a daily is also a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a daily is a domestic cleaner who comes in every day.

clue.text: Cultivated rose

definitions.meaning: to grow plants is to cultivate them, past tense
rose is the past tense of rise; increased

explanation.definitionFit: Grew is the past tense of grow, which can mean raising crops or increasing.

clue.text: Spy Rebecca moving to online world

indicators.note: moving the letters around produces a new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A spy named Rebecca relocates to the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberspace is the notional realm of the internet, the digital or online world.
